prompt: A single wide laboratory tableau shows an English sentence entering a mechanical slicer that emits a short row of vividly colored token tiles (whole words, word-pieces, spaces and punctuation), while a long unfurling document is simultaneously diced into a towering heap of tens of thousands of the same tiles; the tiles travel two parallel conveyor belts labeled “input / prompt” (modest price-per-million) and “output / generation” (steeper price, annotated “more compute”), both dumping into a cash register that totals millions of tokens; beside the register two identical finished reports sit, one produced by a bargain-priced but rambling model whose extra token mountain has equaled the bill of a costlier concise model, a large overlay calculator multiplying token price by tokens actually spent and labeling the result “cost per completed task.”
